back: A pasture sown or planted with selected, productive grasses and legumes and managed with fertiliser, weed control and controlled grazing.
Leaves, shoots and pods of shrubs and trees eaten by livestock, especially goats.

front: Value of grasses, legumes and browse
back: Grasses: energy and bulk. Legumes: protein and nitrogen fixation. Browse: green, protein-rich feed in the dry season.
Sweet veld keeps its feeding value when dry; sour veld is palatable only when young and green.
To supply the correct Rhizobium bacteria so nodules form and fix nitrogen.
Choose site; test and lime soil; fine firm seedbed; choose species and certified seed; phosphorus at sowing; sow shallow and roll; weed control; light first grazing.

front: When is a new pasture first grazed?
back: Lightly and briefly, once plants are firmly rooted and not pulled out when tugged.

front: Seed or fertiliser for a field
back: kg needed = rate (kg/ha) × area (ha); area in ha = m² ÷ 10,000.
